text: There are only three reasons why things do not happen the way you want them to happen as a leader.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Lenny asks Anuj about leadership and managing teams effectively. Anuj explains his framework for diagnosing performance issues when team members aren't delivering expected results. He breaks down the root causes into three categories: capability gaps (can't do), motivation/alignment problems (won't do), or systemic setup failures (weren't set up to do). This framework helps leaders identify whether they need to coach, realign, or fix organizational processes.
text_ko: 리더로서 일이 원하는 대로 안 되는 건 세 가지 이유밖에 없어요. 첫째, 그 사람이 그 일을 못해서, 즉 능력 문제(capability issue)이에요. 둘째, 그 사람이 하려 하지 않아서, 즉 동기나 조율(alignment) 문제예요. 셋째, 그 사람이 하도록 환경이나 시스템을 못 만들어줘서인데, 이건 당신 책임이에요 — 업무 방식(ways of working)이나 설계(design)를 제대로 해놓지 않았기 때문이에요.
text_zh: 作为领导，事情没有按你预期发展，无非就三个原因。你看一个人，要么是他能力不行，做不了；要么是他不想做，动机或者目标不一致的问题；要么就是你没给他搭好台子，工作流程和机制设计有问题，这其实是你自己的责任。
text_es: Solo hay tres razones por las que las cosas no salen como quieres cuando eres líder. Puedes mirar a una persona y decir: o esa persona no puede hacerlo, que es un tema de capacidades, o no quiere hacerlo, que es un problema de motivación o alineación, o no se le dieron las condiciones para hacerlo, y ahí el problema es tuyo porque no diseñaste bien los procesos de trabajo desde el principio.
key_sentence: There are only three reasons why things do not happen the way you want them to happen as a leader.
original_text: There are only three reasons why things do not happen the way you want them to happen as a leader. You can look at a person, and you would say either that person can't do, which is a capability issue, or they won't do, which is a motivation or an alignment issue, or they were not set up to do, which is really your problem that you didn't set up the ways of working now design properly.

vocabulary.definition: The process of identifying the nature or cause of a problem or issue.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, diagnosing is crucial for troubleshooting performance issues, ensuring that teams can address root causes effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with medical contexts, in business it implies a systematic approach to problem-solving rather than a casual assessment.

vocabulary.definition: Problems that hinder an individual or organization's ability to achieve desired outcomes or operate efficiently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, performance issues may relate to employee productivity, software functionality, or operational processes that fail to meet established benchmarks.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting a need for improvement or intervention, and should be used with sensitivity.

vocabulary.definition: The anticipated outcomes or objectives that an individual or organization aims to achieve through specific actions or strategies.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management and strategic planning, defining expected results is essential for measuring success and aligning team efforts with organizational goals.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase implies a level of planning and foresight, and should be used in contexts where clear objectives have been established.

vocabulary.definition: A structured approach or system that provides a foundation for understanding or addressing a particular issue or set of issues.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, frameworks are often used to guide decision-making, project management, and strategic planning, helping teams align their efforts with overarching goals.
vocabulary.nuance: While frameworks provide guidance, they should be flexible enough to adapt to changing circumstances and should not be seen as rigid rules.

text: One of the things that I realized once we started working with the products is that product managers and generally, companies are too engrossed in thinking about... because they are very close to the product.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Lenny asks Anuj about his approach to building user experiences for new users. Anuj explains a common bias that product managers develop - they become so immersed in their product that they assume users share their level of engagement and understanding. He argues this creates a disconnect because most consumers don't think about any single product constantly and need to be approached differently when they first encounter a product.
text_ko: 제품(product)과 함께 일해보면서 깨달은 것 중 하나는 프로덕트 매니저(product manager)들이나 회사들이 제품에 너무 몰입해 있다는 거예요. 제품이 워낙 가깝고 마음에 닿아 있어서 항상 들여다보니까 작동 방식이나 사용감 같은 사소한 뉘앙스까지 계속 신경 쓰게 되죠. 그리고 거기에는 거의 본질적으로 '모두가 하루 종일, 항상 이 제품만 생각하고 있을 거다'라는 편향이 깔려 있어요, 등등.
text_zh: 我发现一个问题，就是当我们开始接触这些产品的时候，产品经理们，包括整个公司，都太沉浸在产品里了...因为他们跟产品贴得太近，把产品当心头肉一样，天天盯着看。他们会去扣很多细节，比如这个功能怎么用啊，体验感觉怎么样啊，这样就不知不觉陷入了一个误区，觉得所有人都会像他们一样，一天到晚想着这个产品。
text_es: Una de las cosas de las que me di cuenta cuando empezamos a trabajar con los productos es que los product managers y, en general, las empresas se obsesionan demasiado pensando en... porque están muy pegados al producto. Lo sienten como algo muy suyo, y lo están viendo todo el tiempo. Se fijan en un montón de detalles pequeños sobre cómo funciona y se siente, y casi sin darse cuenta caen en el sesgo (bias) de pensar que todo el mundo está pensando en este producto las 24 horas del día, que es su prioridad número uno, y así sucesivamente.
key_sentence: Companies are too engrossed in their product, missing broader perspectives.
original_text: One of the things that I realized once we started working with the products is that product managers and generally, companies are too engrossed in thinking about... because they are very close to the product. It's close to their heart, and they're looking at it all the time. They're looking at a lot of minor nuances in terms of how this works and feels, and almost inherent into this is the bias that everybody is thinking about this product all day, all the time, and so on, and so forth.

vocabulary.definition: Deeply engaged or involved in a particular activity or subject.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being immersed often refers to a team or individual who is fully dedicated to understanding a product, market, or customer needs.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'immersed' conveys a positive connotation of dedication, it can imply a lack of perspective if one is too absorbed in a single focus.

vocabulary.definition: A tendency to favor one perspective or outcome over others, often leading to a lack of impartiality.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, bias can affect decision-making, product development, and market research, potentially skewing results and outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: Bias often carries a negative connotation, suggesting unfairness or prejudice; however, it can also refer to legitimate preferences based on data or experience.

vocabulary.definition: To accept something as true without proof or verification.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business environments, assumptions are often made in strategic planning, risk assessment, and project management, which can lead to significant consequences if incorrect.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'assume' is commonly used in everyday language, in a business context, it can imply a lack of thorough analysis or due diligence.

vocabulary.definition: Professionals responsible for the strategy, roadmap, and feature definition of a product or product line.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product managers play a crucial role in bridging the gap between engineering, marketing, and customer needs to ensure successful product development.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'product managers' implies a leadership role that requires both technical knowledge and strong interpersonal skills; it is not interchangeable with roles focused solely on engineering or marketing.

text: There's very interesting insight that I heard from Scott Belsky from Adobe, and then now, he's doing very interesting stuff, and that stayed with me which was you have to think about users on modern internet consumers having three attributes.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Anuj continues explaining his philosophy for designing products for new users. He shares a framework from Adobe's Scott Belsky that characterizes internet users with three key traits. According to this framework, users are 'lazy' (don't want to spend time learning), 'vain' (resistant to changing existing habits), and 'selfish' (need clear personal benefits). This insight helps product managers design onboarding experiences that account for user reluctance and skepticism.
text_ko: Adobe의 Scott Belsky에게서 들은 흥미로운 인사이트가 있어요. 지금 그가 하는 일도 정말 흥미로운데, 그가 한 말 중 하나가 오래 남았어요. 현대 인터넷 소비자(modern internet consumers)를 생각할 때 세 가지 특성이 있다고 보라는 거예요. 즉, 게으르고, 허영심이 많고, 이기적이에요.
text_zh: 我听Adobe的Scott Belsky说过一个特别有意思的观点，他现在在做的东西也很有意思，这个观点一直让我印象深刻。他说你得这样看现在的互联网用户，他们有三个特点：懒、爱慕虚荣，还有就是自私。
text_es: Hay una reflexión muy interesante que escuché de Scott Belsky de Adobe, que ahora está haciendo cosas súper interesantes, y se me quedó grabada: tienes que pensar en los usuarios, en los consumidores modernos de internet, como si tuvieran tres características. O sea, son flojos, son vanidosos y son egoístas.
key_sentence: Modern internet consumers are lazy, vain, and selfish, which stayed with me.
original_text: There's very interesting insight that I heard from Scott Belsky from Adobe, and then now, he's doing very interesting stuff, and that stayed with me which was you have to think about users on modern internet consumers having three attributes. So they are lazy, they are vain, and they're selfish.

vocabulary.definition: A deep understanding of a complex situation or problem, often leading to new perspectives or solutions.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, insights are crucial for making informed decisions, driving innovation, and understanding customer behavior.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'insight' implies a valuable understanding, it is often used to suggest a revelation that can significantly impact strategy or operations.

vocabulary.definition: Characteristics or qualities that define or describe an individual, object, or concept.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, attributes are often used to analyze products, customer segments, or employee skills to enhance decision-making and strategy.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'attributes' can imply both inherent qualities and those that can be developed or influenced over time.

vocabulary.definition: A structured approach or system that provides a foundation for understanding or addressing a particular issue.
vocabulary.businessContext: Frameworks are commonly employed in business to guide strategic planning, project management, and problem-solving processes.
vocabulary.nuance: Using 'framework' suggests a systematic and organized method, which can be more effective than ad-hoc approaches.

vocabulary.definition: To describe the distinctive qualities or features of someone or something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, to characterize a market, product, or consumer segment helps in tailoring strategies and communications effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a detailed and nuanced description, which can be critical in differentiating between similar entities.

text: We are product managers, and we are in the business of influence. Users are doing something, and now we want them to do something else. Our engineers are doing something, and now we want to influence them into building something fast.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Lenny asks Anuj about effective messaging and value propositions for users. Anuj reframes the entire role of product management as fundamentally being about influence - not just influencing users to adopt products, but also influencing engineers to build features quickly and leadership to approve plans. He argues that viewing product management through this lens of influence helps PMs think more strategically about how they approach all their relationships.
text_ko: 우리는 프로덕트 매니저(product managers)로서 영향력을 행사하는 일을 해요. 사용자들은 지금 어떤 행동을 하고 있고, 우리는 그들이 다른 행동을 하도록 유도하려고 해요. 엔지니어들(engineers)은 지금 뭔가를 하고 있고, 우리는 그들을 설득해 빠르게 뭔가를 만들게 하려 해요. 사실 리더십(leadership)은 이미 계획이 있고, 우리가 하는 건 결국 그들이 그 계획을 보고 승인(sign off)해서 다른 일을 하게 만드는 거예요. 우리는 영향력을 발휘하는 일을 하고 있고, 여러분도 사내에서 늘 이 일을 하고 있어요.
text_zh: 我们是产品经理，说白了就是干影响别人这一行的。用户现在在做这个，我们想让他们去做那个。我们的工程师现在在搞这个，我们得想办法影响他们快点把东西做出来。还有领导层那边，他们有自己的计划，我们得影响他们看看我们的方案，基本上就是让他们点个头，然后去做别的事儿。我们就是干影响这一行的，而且你在公司内部天天都在做这种事。
text_es: Somos product managers, y nuestro negocio es la influencia. Los usuarios están haciendo algo, y ahora queremos que hagan otra cosa. Nuestros ingenieros están haciendo algo, y queremos influenciarlos para que construyan algo rápido. En realidad, el liderazgo tiene ciertos planes. Los vamos a influenciar para que, básicamente, revisen un plan, le den el visto bueno, y hagan algo diferente. Estamos en el negocio de la influencia, y tú estás haciendo esto todo el tiempo internamente.
key_sentence: We are in the business of influence, wanting users and engineers to sign off.
original_text: We are product managers, and we are in the business of influence. Users are doing something, and now we want them to do something else. Our engineers are doing something, and now we want to influence them into building something fast. Really, leadership has some plans. We'll influence them to, essentially, look at a plan, and basically, sign off, and do something else. We are in the business of influence, and you are doing this all the time internally.

vocabulary.definition: The capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, influence often refers to the ability of product managers to sway user behavior or engineer decisions to align with strategic goals.
vocabulary.nuance: While influence can imply persuasion, it often carries a connotation of subtlety rather than overt coercion.

vocabulary.definition: A statement that summarizes why a consumer should choose a product or service, highlighting its unique benefits and value.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups and tech, crafting compelling value propositions is essential for attracting customers and differentiating offerings in a competitive market.
vocabulary.nuance: Value propositions should be clear and customer-focused, avoiding jargon to ensure they resonate with the target audience.

vocabulary.definition: In a basic and essential way; at the core or foundation of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In discussions about product changes or strategy, 'fundamentally' is often used to emphasize core principles that should not be altered.
vocabulary.nuance: This term suggests a deep-seated importance, making it suitable for discussions about core values or essential changes.

vocabulary.definition: The process of overseeing the development, marketing, and lifecycle of a product from conception to market delivery.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, product management is critical for aligning product development with user needs and business objectives, ensuring successful product launches.
vocabulary.nuance: This term encompasses both strategic and tactical aspects, making it important to differentiate between high-level vision and day-to-day operations.

text: The other part that I found interesting here is that I really truly believe in the power of three. So I actually ask my teams to write three press releases, alternative and divergent like, 'What if we...' Suppose you're launching a membership program.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Lenny asks about how Anuj operationalizes the 'working backwards' process from Amazon's playbook. Beyond writing a single press release, Anuj explains his approach of creating three divergent press releases for any major product decision. Each press release explores a fundamentally different strategic direction - for example, when launching a membership program, one might explore different tier structures while another might explore a completely different approach like points-based pricing.
text_ko: 여기서 제가 흥미롭게 본 또 하나는, 저는 정말로 '세의 힘'을 믿는다는 거예요. 그래서 팀들에게는 '만약 우리가 이랬다면…' 같은 식으로 대안적이고 서로 다른 관점에서 보도자료(press releases) 세 가지를 써보라고 요청해요. 예를 들어 멤버십 프로그램(membership program)을 런칭한다고 치면, 티어(tiers)를 두 개로 하지 말고 세 개로 해보자고 하거나, 멤버십을 만드는 대신 티어 기반 가격제(tiered pricing program)에 멤버십 포인트(membership points)를 도입해보자는 식이에요.
text_zh: 还有一点我觉得特别有意思，就是我真的很相信"三"的力量。所以我会让团队写三个不同的新闻稿，每个都是完全不同的思路，就像"如果我们这样做会怎样..."比如说你要推出会员项目吧，那与其只做两个等级，咱们就做三个等级，或者换个思路，与其做普通会员制，不如搞个分层定价的积分会员制。
text_es: Lo otro que me parece súper interesante es que realmente creo en el poder del tres. Entonces lo que hago es pedirles a mis equipos que escriban tres comunicados de prensa, pero alternativos y divergentes, como "¿Y si...?" Supongamos que van a lanzar un programa de membresía. Entonces, en lugar de dos niveles, hagamos tres niveles, o por ejemplo, tomemos otra opción que sería en lugar de crear una membresía, armemos un programa de precios escalonados con puntos de membresía.
key_sentence: I believe in the power of three; ask teams for alternative and divergent ideas.
original_text: The other part that I found interesting here is that I really truly believe in the power of three. So I actually ask my teams to write three press releases, alternative and divergent like, 'What if we...' Suppose you're launching a membership program. So, instead of two tiers, let's do three tiers, or for example, let's take another one which is instead of building a membership, let's build up tiering pricing program with membership points.

vocabulary.definition: To put a concept or plan into action or practice, making it functional and applicable in real-world scenarios.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, operationalizing often refers to translating strategic goals into actionable tasks and processes that can be implemented by teams.
vocabulary.nuance: This term carries a connotation of practicality and execution, suggesting that a theoretical idea is being made tangible and usable.

vocabulary.definition: Describing ideas, paths, or approaches that are different or varied from a common point or standard.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, divergent thinking is encouraged during brainstorming sessions to foster creativity and innovation by exploring multiple perspectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While divergent can imply a positive exploration of alternatives, it may also suggest a lack of focus if not managed properly.

vocabulary.definition: A structured initiative that offers exclusive benefits or services to individuals who pay a fee or meet specific criteria to join.
vocabulary.businessContext: Membership programs are commonly used in businesses to build customer loyalty, enhance engagement, and generate recurring revenue through subscription models.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often implies a sense of community and belonging, which can enhance customer retention and satisfaction.

vocabulary.definition: An official statement issued to media outlets to announce news or developments related to an organization, product, or event.
vocabulary.businessContext: Press releases are a key tool in public relations and marketing, used to communicate important information and generate media coverage for a company.
vocabulary.nuance: While press releases are formal communications, they should be crafted to engage the audience and convey the significance of the news effectively.

text: Unless you really... and I'm not saying you need to be an authority of that.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Lenny asks about Anuj's philosophy that product managers should be more 'full-stack' than most currently are. Anuj explains that successful PMs must either develop deep expertise across multiple disciplines (marketing, engineering, business) or build strong partnerships with experts in those areas. He emphasizes that PMs can't succeed by focusing only on their narrow product area - they need to understand and influence the full ecosystem that makes products successful.
text_ko: 솔직히 말해서... 제가 말하는 건 그 분야의 권위자(authority)가 될 필요는 없다는 거예요. 그걸 정말, 정말 잘하든가, 아니면 파트너십(partnerships)을 잘 구축해서 아이디어나 제품을 그분들한테 시험해 보고 피드백(feedback)을 충분히 받아 그 의견을 반영해 최종 결정을 내리지 않으면 성공하기 어렵다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 除非你真的...我不是说你必须是那方面的权威啊。要么你在那方面特别特别厉害，要么你建立了合作关系，把你的想法或产品拿给那些人过过眼，听听他们的意见，最后在那个环节做决定，不然的话，我觉得你很难成功。
text_es: A menos que realmente... y no digo que tengas que ser un experto en eso. O eres muy, muy bueno en eso, or has construido alianzas estratégicas (partnerships), y has pasado tus ideas o producto por esas personas y has obtenido su opinión fundamentada, y finalmente has tomado una decisión basada en eso, no creo que vayas a tener mucho éxito.
key_sentence: Unless you really... and I'm not saying you need to be an authority of that.
original_text: Unless you really... and I'm not saying you need to be an authority of that. Either you are very, very good at that, or you have built partnerships, and have run your ideas or product through those people and gotten weighted from them, and finally made a decision around that part, I don't think you'll be very successful.

vocabulary.definition: The power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience. It can also refer to a person or organization having control or influence in a specific area.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, authority often pertains to leadership roles where individuals are responsible for guiding teams and making strategic decisions. It can also refer to subject matter experts whose opinions are highly regarded in their fields.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'authority' implies a level of respect and recognition, it can also suggest a hierarchical structure that may not always be welcomed in collaborative environments.

vocabulary.definition: A high level of knowledge or skill in a particular area, often acquired through education and experience. It denotes proficiency and competence.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, expertise is crucial for innovation and problem-solving, as organizations often rely on specialists to drive projects and initiatives. It can also enhance credibility in negotiations and client interactions.
vocabulary.nuance: Expertise suggests not only knowledge but also the ability to apply that knowledge effectively; it is generally more respected than mere experience.

vocabulary.definition: A set of beliefs or principles that guide behavior and decision-making. It encompasses the underlying values and attitudes that shape an organization's culture.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, philosophy can refer to a company's mission statement, core values, and overall approach to operations and strategy. It influences how decisions are made and how employees interact with each other and clients.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'philosophy' can imply a theoretical framework, it is often practical in nature, guiding real-world actions and policies within an organization.

vocabulary.definition: Achieving desired aims or attaining prosperity, often measured by specific outcomes such as profitability, growth, or market share. It denotes a favorable outcome in endeavors.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, success is typically evaluated through metrics such as revenue growth, customer satisfaction, and market position. It reflects the effectiveness of strategies and operations.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'successful' can vary in meaning depending on the goals set by an organization, and it may not always correlate with traditional measures of success like financial gain.

text: So we essentially saw that if a startup actually usually wants to do a bunch of things across the border, there's always like, 'Hey, I should be investing in tech debt or building core platforms. That would really help my product in the long term.
speaker: Anuj Rathi
context: Lenny asks Anuj to explain his 'four BB framework' for product strategy. Anuj describes how startups typically face competing priorities across different types of work. He explains that engineering teams often push for technical infrastructure improvements and paying down tech debt, arguing these investments will benefit products long-term, while product managers want to focus on feature development and user-facing improvements. This tension creates the need for a strategic framework to allocate resources.
text_ko: 결국 우리가 본 건, 스타트업이 여러 분야에서 동시에 뭔가를 하려고 하면 늘 “기술 부채(tech debt)에 투자하거나 코어 플랫폼(core platforms)을 만들어야 해. 장기적으로 제품에 큰 도움이 되고, 이건 정말 중요해”라는 얘기가 나온다는 거예요. 주로 엔지니어링 매니저들(engineering managers)이나 그런 여력(bandwidth)을 요구하는 분들이죠.
text_zh: 所以我们基本上发现，如果一个初创公司想要跨境做很多事情，总是会有这样的声音：'嘿，我应该投资技术债务(tech debt)或者搭建核心平台。这对我的产品长远发展真的很有帮助，超级重要。'而且我的工程经理们，还有很多人都在要这个资源。
text_es: Entonces básicamente vimos que si una startup quiere hacer muchas cosas a nivel internacional, siempre surge como "Oye, debería estar invirtiendo en deuda técnica (tech debt) o construyendo plataformas centrales. Eso realmente ayudaría a mi producto a largo plazo. Es súper importante," y esos son mis gerentes de ingeniería y en general, la gente pidiendo ese ancho de banda (bandwidth).
key_sentence: if a startup actually usually wants to do a bunch of things across the border
original_text: So we essentially saw that if a startup actually usually wants to do a bunch of things across the border, there's always like, 'Hey, I should be investing in tech debt or building core platforms. vocabulary.definition: The act of allocating resources, usually money, with the expectation of generating an income or profit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and startup environments, investing often refers to funding projects, technologies, or assets that are expected to yield future returns.
vocabulary.nuance: While investing typically implies a financial commitment, it can also encompass time and effort directed towards growth opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: Fundamental systems or technologies that serve as the backbone for applications or services within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, core platforms are essential for developing products and ensuring scalability, reliability, and integration with other services.
vocabulary.nuance: The term suggests a foundational importance, indicating that these platforms are critical for operational success and should be prioritized in development.

vocabulary.definition: Situations where multiple tasks or objectives require attention and resources, often leading to conflicts in decision-making.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a startup, leaders frequently face competing priorities when balancing product development, customer acquisition, and operational efficiency.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase highlights the challenges of resource allocation and strategic focus, suggesting the need for careful management and prioritization.

vocabulary.definition: A time frame that extends into the future, typically beyond one year, focusing on sustainability and enduring outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business strategy, long-term considerations are crucial for planning investments, growth trajectories, and overall vision.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a broader perspective, emphasizing the importance of patience and foresight in achieving lasting success.
